overview: Dolwyddelan preserves a Welsh princely building programme associated with Llywelyn ap Iorwerth, alongside later alterations made under English control.

items.text: Llywelyn ap Iorwerth, ruler of Gwynedd in the early thirteenth century, used fortresses to command mountain routes.
Dolwyddelan's surviving fabric requires separation from later additions when reconstructing his building programme.
English forces took the castle in 1283. The date concerns this fortress and must not substitute for every political transition in Gwynedd.
Edward I altered the keep and added a tower; nineteenth-century restoration changed its appearance again.
